newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish business group welcomes Senate's tax rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish business group welcomes Senate's tax rates.

text.p: Poland's Business Centre Club (BCC), an influential employers' group, cautiously welcomed the Senate's decision on Thursday to cut personal income tax levels by one point next year.

BCC President Marek Goliszewski told a news conference his group was pleased that the Senate rejected lower house's rates of 17, 20, 33 and 45 percent but added taxes in general were not low enough to sufficiently spur Polish economic growth.

"We took the Senate's decision positively of course...but it's necessary to say that the rates that were proposed by the Senate were not the rates of 20, 30 and 40 percent, once promised for 1997," Goliszewski said.

He said such rates would help Poland double economic growth from current levels. The country's gross domestic product is seen coming closer to five percent this year after last year's seven-percent-growth.
Poland's tax rates were at 20, 30 and 40 percent in 1994, under a budget written by the centre-right predecessors of the currently ruling left-wing.
The ruling coalition of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Polish Peasant Party (PSL) raised taxes for 1995, especially for high earners, but promised later decreases.
BCC deputy president Jeremi Mordaszewicz, also present, said the budget defecit relative to GDP was decreasing, but not quickly enough considering Poland's rate of economic growth.
The Senate's proposal sees the deficit at 2.8 percent of GDP. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
